title: Extraction and analysis of primary metabolites during Xanthomonas-Barley interaction
author: Veronica Roman-Reyna

steps.title: Grow barley plants
steps.instruction: Sow Barley cv. Morex seeds in Promix soil, incubate at 20 °C and 60 % humidity; grow for three weeks until plants have at least two fully developed leaves (youngest fully expanded leaf will be used).

steps.title: Prepare bacterial cultures
steps.instruction: Retrieve Xanthomonas translucens pv. undulosa (UPB513) and pv. translucens (UPB886) from –80 °C glycerol stock; plate on nutrient agar (3 g/L beef extract, 5 g/L peptone, 15 g/L agar) a week before the experiment and incubate at 28 °C. Three days before inoculation, streak a single colony onto fresh nutrient agar and incubate again at 28 °C.

steps.title: Make inoculum at OD0.1
steps.instruction: On the day of inoculation, suspend a bacterial loop from each strain in sterile water and adjust the suspension to an absorbance of 0.1 at 600 nm (≈10⁸ CFU/mL).

steps.title: Inoculate barley leaves
steps.instruction: Fill a 1 mL needleless (insulin‑type) syringe with bacterial suspension or mock water, press the syringe against the abaxial surface of the youngest fully expanded leaf of three‑week‑old plants, place a finger on the opposite side to keep firm contact, and gently plunge to infiltrate 2 mL. Inoculate at least 30–40 leaves per strain.

steps.title: Collect and clean leaves
steps.instruction: At 6 h, 12 h, and 24 h post‑inoculation, cut pools of four leaves at the base, rinse each leaf with 75 % ethanol to eliminate surface microorganisms, and weigh the pool.

steps.title: Vacuum infiltrate ribitol
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 ppm ribitol solution; place each leaf pool in a vacuum chamber and infiltrate with the ribitol solution. After infiltration, re‑weigh the leaves to calculate infiltrated water volume (assuming water density 1 g/mL).

steps.title: Extract apoplastic fluid
steps.instruction: Using 50 mL syringes to generate negative pressure, extract apoplastic fluid from each leaf pool following the Roman‑Reyna and Rathjen 2017 protocol. At each time point, plate 2 µL of the fluid on nutrient agar to determine CFU (expected 5–200 CFU). Flash‑freeze the remaining fluid to prevent metabolite degradation.

steps.title: Select comparable pools
steps.instruction: From each time point, choose four leaf pools that have similar CFU counts for downstream metabolite analysis.

steps.title: Extract metabolites
steps.instruction: Mix 500 µL of apoplastic fluid with 1 mL of methanol:chloroform:water (5:2:2, v/v/v); vortex, incubate 5 min at 28 °C with shaking at 20 rpm; centrifuge at 2200 g, 15 °C for 15 min; collect the upper methanol‑water phase and keep 200 µL for analysis.

steps.title: Derivatize extracts
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of ACN:IPA:H₂O (3:3:2, v/v/v) to the sample; dry half of the extract to completeness; add 10 µL of 40 mg/mL methoxyamine in pyridine and shake at 30 °C for 1.5 h; then add 91 µL of MSTFA + FAMEs and shake at 37 °C for 0.5 h.

steps.title: Submit samples for GC‑TOF MS
steps.instruction: Send 200 µL of the upper phase (or the derivatized extract) to the West Coast Metabolomics Center (UC Davis) for untargeted primary metabolism analysis by GC‑TOF MS using the assay “Primary Metabolism by GC‑TOF MS: carbohydrates and sugar phosphates, amino acids, hydroxyl acids, free fatty acids, purines, pyrimidines, aromatics”.
